back: Database is fully managed with no Agent and no instance features. Managed Instance gives near-complete instance compatibility inside a VNet. Keyword: instance features decide.

front: When SQL Server on Azure VMs
back: A specific SQL version, a feature neither PaaS option has, or OS and filesystem access. Keyword: you need the box.
Very large databases with backup and restore times independent of size. vCore model only. Keyword: size stops mattering.
Auto-pauses and bills per second — the answer for a database idle for long periods. Keyword: intermittent workload.
Many databases sharing a resource budget, for unpredictable non-overlapping peaks. Keyword: bursty and many.
Moves a whole partition in or out as a metadata operation — the real reason to partition. Keyword: manageability, not speed.
Page includes row plus prefix and dictionary compression. Both trade CPU for less IO and memory. Keyword: page is more.
Data Migration Assistant reports breaking changes against the target — skipping it is how an unsupported feature is found after cutover. Keyword: assess first.
Offline takes the source out of service and is simpler. Online synchronises until cutover at the cost of complexity. Keyword: downtime window decides.

front: Entra admin should be a group
back: So responsibility survives an individual leaving. Keyword: group, not person.
Authenticates against the database rather than a server login, which makes the database portable — and is what failover groups need. Keyword: portable.
Protects files at rest, transparent to anyone querying — so it does not hide data from an administrator. Keyword: not against DBAs.
The client encrypts and decrypts; the engine only sees ciphertext. The only option that hides values from an administrator. Keyword: keys outside the database.
Deterministic allows equality and grouping but reveals patterns. Randomised is stronger and permits no operations. Keyword: query or hide.
Allow comparison and pattern matching on Always Encrypted columns inside protected memory. VBS enclaves are the virtualisation-based form. Keyword: query the encrypted.
Permits traffic from any Azure resource in any subscription — not just yours. Frequently left on from testing. Keyword: wider than it sounds.
Obscures values in results for unprivileged users. A presentation control, not a security boundary. Keyword: not encryption.
A predicate function bound to a table, enforced by the engine on every query. Keyword: filter rows per user.
Cryptographic tamper evidence — proves alteration was or was not made. Integrity, not confidentiality. Keyword: prove it wasn't changed.
Database-level auditing on top of server-level produces duplicate records. Keyword: pick one level.
Without one, a CPU figure is a number rather than evidence. Keyword: compare against what.
What is running now, including the blocking session id. Keyword: right now.
The lightweight tracing framework that replaced SQL Profiler; use it on anything in production. Keyword: Profiler is retired.
Plan regression — a plan changed and performance dropped, so force the previous plan. Keyword: it was fast last week.
Forces the last good plan without human intervention and reverts if it does not help. Built on Query Store. Keyword: self-correcting.
Blocking is one session waiting on another. A deadlock is mutual and the engine kills a victim. Keyword: waiting vs unresolvable.
A per-query hint that ignores write cost and existing indexes — a starting point, not an instruction. Keyword: don't apply blindly.
Suggests a missing included column on the index being seeked. Keyword: cover the query.
Reorganise at moderate fragmentation, rebuild at high. Online rebuilds keep the table available. Keyword: by fragmentation level.
Caps CPU, memory, and IO per workload group so one query cannot starve everything else. Keyword: ring-fence the workload.
Intelligent query processing features arrive with the database compatibility level — so raising it is a performance change to test. Keyword: test the level change.

front: No SQL Agent on Azure SQL Database
back: Agent exists on SQL Server and Managed Instance only — a consequential difference when migrating. Keyword: jobs must be rehomed.
Run T-SQL across a target group — a server, a pool, or a named list of databases. The Agent replacement for Azure SQL Database. Keyword: many databases, one script.
How Agent notifies operators of job failure. No mail profile means silent failures. Keyword: configure notifications.
Job history and step output — a job failing without detail usually has no output file configured. Keyword: log the step.
ARM and Bicep for reproducible environments; PowerShell and CLI for scripted conditional work. Keyword: reproducible means declarative.
Compares desired schema against the target and generates the difference. Keyword: state-based schema deployment.
A name that is not globally unique, a region without the requested service objective, or a firewall rule locking out the agent. Keyword: check the obvious three.
Azure Automation runbooks, Logic Apps, or a timer-triggered Function. Keyword: not everything is a query.
RPO says how much data may be lost — synchronous or not. RTO says how fast — warm standby or not. Keyword: read for the two numbers.
Geo-replication gives readable secondaries with manual failover. A failover group adds a listener and automatic failover. Keyword: the listener.
Automatic failover during a transient outage can be worse than the outage itself. Keyword: don't flap.

front: Point-in-time restore creates a new database
back: It never overwrites the original — a surprise best discovered before an incident. Keyword: new database.
Weekly, monthly, and yearly backups kept up to ten years, beyond the 35-day PITR window. Keyword: beyond 35 days.
Allows point-in-time recovery and requires log backups — their absence is why a log grows until the disk fills. Keyword: back up the log.
Last full, last differential, then logs in order, with NORECOVERY on all but the last. Keyword: recover only at the end.
An availability group replicates databases between instances. An FCI moves a whole instance over shared storage. Keyword: databases vs instance.
In Azure an AG listener needs a load balancer or distributed network name, or it cannot be reached. Keyword: listener needs plumbing.
Synchronous gives zero data loss within a region; asynchronous is used across regions and accepts loss. Keyword: distance forces async.

front: An untested plan is a guess
back: A scheduled failover test turns an assumed recovery time into a measured one. Keyword: exercise it.
